I am old now, eighty years, and my small piece of land is only a little bit — I plant my cassava and cocoyam the way my mother taught me. I don't buy the white man's fertilizer; it costs too much money and I don't trust it on my tubers. I put the goat droppings and the kitchen ash on the ground, and I use the cassava stems I kept from last year like my neighbors do. My hands are slow now, so my daughter and her children come to help me weed and harvest.
